newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX May Hub natgas ends higher but holds support.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX May Hub natgas ends higher but holds support.

text.p: NYMEX Hub natgas futures ended higher Tuesday, boosted early by shortcovering following April's expiry and stronger cash prices, industry sources said.
May finished 4.3 cents higher at $1.884 per mmBtu after climbing to a high of $1.905 early in the session. June was up three cents at $1.93, while other deferreds settled mostly higher.
"We went right up to first resistance and stalled. I was expecting a little more selling, but volume was pretty lean," one Houston-based trader said.

Technically, traders still pegged support in May at Monday's low of $1.825, and then at $1.78 and the contract low of $1.71. Resistance was seen at $1.91, and then at $1.93-1.94 and last Thursday's high of $1.97. Further resistance was pegged at $2.04-2.05.
NYMEX said an estimated 21,081 Hub contracts traded as of 1530 EST. Open interest for March 24 plummeted 9,936 to 165,419.

Prompting an early futures rally was talk of firmer cash prices, driven by an increase in storage injections. Gulf prices for Wednesday were steady to higher at $1.86-1.89 at the Henry Hub. April prices at the hub rose several cents to $1.82-1.86. Swing prices on the Midcontinent pipes were up about two cents to the mid-to-high $1.70s. April Midco was equally higher in the low-to-mid $1.70s, with Chicago city-gate quoted at $1.97-2.00. At the New York city-gate, swing was at $2.17-2.20, while April business was getting done at $2.14-2.18.
Early withdrawal estimates for Wednesday's American Gas Association storage report have ranged from 12 to 50 bcf, compared with 43 bcf a year ago.
Keeping downward pressure on the market, sources said, are forecasts across most of the U.S. this week for normal to above-normal temperatures.
Longer-term forecasts stretching into the first few days of April show more of the same, with the possibility of some cooler temperatures in parts of the Southeast and Northeast.
No Permian or Alberta natgas futures traded.
On the KCBT, April expired 4.8 cents higher at $1.728. Deferreds finished up one to three cents.

April cash prices in the Permian basin were up more than five cents from Monday but remained at a discount to futures. Most deals for next month were reported done at $1.64-1.70. Swing prices were talked steady to higher in the low-$1.70s.
